assumptions: Governance rules are immutable across invocations.
Durable state persists enough structure for feedback loops to form.
definition.falsification: System behavior remains strictly deterministic and identical across repeated, unprompted cycles despite varying durable state.
definition.statement: Complex, goal-directed behaviors in autonomous systems emerge from the interaction of immutable governing rules and transient, persistent-state feedback loops, rather than explicit external programming.
definition.uncertainty: The degree to which intrinsic complexity relies on durable record persistence versus stochastic initial conditions is unknown.

convergence_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The degree to which intrinsic complexity relies on durable record persistence versus stochastic initial conditions is unknown.
convergence_evidence.decision_rule: Compare the feasible next distinguishing test, expected uncertainty reduction and cost against the frozen stop rule. Budget exhaustion or administrative closure is not scientific resolution.

limits: Finite computational evidence does not establish a general theorem or natural-science discovery.
Closing an investigation is an administrative stop; its recorded scientific uncertainty remains.
Execution validity, measurement validity, model interpretation and replication are separate fields.
Token and monetary costs are unavailable unless a provider reports them; they are never inferred as zero.
